items.abstract: Background: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in CYP21A2. Although well-established genotype-phenotype correlations exist for the common pseudogene-derived alleles, next-generation sequencing increasingly identifies rare missense variants whose clinical significance is unknown, which hampers classification, counselling and the selection of patients for new targeted therapies. Methods: We characterized three CYP21A2 missense variants reported in patients with non-classic (NC) or simple-virilizing (SV) CAH, p.A90V (c.269C>T), p.L108Q (c.323T>A) and p.L318M (c.952C>A), together with the intron 2 splice variant c.293-13C>G (I2G) found in trans in two of the patients. Variants were annotated at the gene level with NCBI E-utilities (ClinVar, dbSNP), Ensembl VEP, SpliceAI and AlphaGenome, at the population level with gnomAD v4.1 and the 1000 Genomes Project, and at the protein level with AlphaMissense, REVEL, CADD, MetaRNN, PrimateAI, evolutionary conservation, AlphaFold and FoldX stability calculations mapped on the CYP21A2 crystal structure. Wild-type and variant enzymes were expressed in HEK293T cells, protein levels were quantified by Western blot, and 21-hydroxylase activity was measured with radiolabelled progesterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) followed by thin-layer chromatography. Results: All three missense variants are absent from or singletons in 1.6 million gnomAD alleles, absent from the 1000 Genomes Project and absent from ClinVar, affect residues that are conserved in mammalian orthologues and lie in high-confidence regions of the AlphaFold model (pLDDT 97-99). AlphaMissense classified p.A90V and p.L108Q as likely pathogenic (0.76 and 0.85) but p.L318M as likely benign (0.31), whereas CADD, MetaRNN and REVEL supported deleteriousness for all three; SpliceAI and AlphaGenome excluded a splicing effect of the missense changes but reproduced the acceptor-site loss and cryptic-acceptor activation caused by I2G. In vitro, protein expression was reduced to 52%, 65% and 59% of wild type for p.A90V, p.L108Q and p.L318M. Total 17-OHP 21-hydroxylation was 36.7%, 1.4% and 38.5% of wild type, and total progesterone conversion 24.9%, 9.2% and 17.5%, revealing a substrate-dependent, almost complete loss of function for p.L108Q. FoldX predicted destabilization for p.A90V (ΔΔG 3.2 kcal/mol) and p.L108Q (2.5 kcal/mol) but not for p.L318M (0.1 kcal/mol); structural analysis attributes the severe p.L108Q defect to disruption of the hydrogen-bond network (L108-G111-R427) that anchors the heme propionates. Conclusions: Combining functional assays with gene- and protein-level computational analysis classifies all three variants as pathogenic. p.L108Q is a severe allele consistent with classic SV CAH, which resolves the ambiguous SV/NC classification of the male index patient, whereas p.A90V (homozygous) and p.L318M (in trans with I2G) are mild alleles that explain the NC phenotypes. The data illustrate that AlphaMissense alone would have misclassified p.L318M and that residual activity, not in silico scores, should guide counselling and the selection of patients for CRF1-receptor-antagonist therapy.

items.summary: In medical imaging AI, we commonly assume that diagnostic classifiers will increase in accuracy if they are trained on more data, but in reality, their performance often plateaus. items.abstract: In medical imaging AI, we commonly assume that diagnostic classifiers will increase in accuracy if they are trained on more data, but in reality, their performance often plateaus. To understand this behavior, we ran a spectral analysis of 3D vision transformers, a common supervised deep learning model that can be trained to classify disease based on 3D brain MRI. For simpler classification methods such as linear discriminant analysis, the classifier performance AUC(N), when trained on a sample of size N, is known to depend on the encoder′s eigenspectrum. Each class-discriminative direction in the latent space contributes only after the sample size N reaches a threshold, so the spectrum influences how performance scales with training data. Building on this theory, we show that supervised transformers compress almost all of their discriminative signal into one principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90—0.96): after this representation collapse happens, no further directions cross the threshold as training data increases, and accuracy plateaus. In principle, this plateau in performance could be due to either the encoder′s learned feature space or the difficulty of the task. To distinguish these cases, we trained three types of supervised 3D transformers (ViT3D, MINiT, NIT) and, as a non-collapsing alternative, a frozen self-supervised encoder (DINO), to classify people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus cognitively normal (CN) individuals from 3D brain MRI, using data from the Alzheimer′s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We froze each encoder and applied it to a new task, so that only the task difficulty varied. An easy task encoder (Dementia vs CN), transferred to the harder task (MCI vs CN), did not reproduce the plateau (MINiT threshold 9.2), but full retraining did (2758.5). The plateau is therefore due to the learned encoder, rather than task difficulty. Ranking the feature directions by the proportion of the disease signal they contain, we were able to identify a sign of representation collapse, i.e., a single dominant spike in the latent feature eigenspectrum. This spike was 11—26 times larger than predicted from the rest of the spectrum for the disease-trained (supervised) encoders, but was absent for DINO (0.66). To predict how transformer accuracy scales with the number of training scans, a large spike in the encoder spectrum suggests that the representation has collapsed and additional scans will not help; a small spike means that the signal is spread across many encoder latent space directions, and more training data should boost the classifier performance.

items.abstract: Protein immunogenicity is a major cause of biologic drug failure, leading to the production of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) that accelerate drug clearance, rejection of repeated doses, abolished efficacy, and sometimes life threatening anaphylaxis in patients. These responses constrain the clinical use of synthetic protein therapeutics from non-human origin. To efficiently deimmunize protein therapeutics, we developed a generative discrete diffusion model (MESSI), which takes protein structures as input and outputs sequences that preserve structure without containing peptides predicted to bind major histocompatibility complex class II molecules. MESSI designs sequences with high structural recovery and down to 0 predicted epitopes for specified MHC molecules at higher efficiency than post-hoc filtering approaches. Experimentally, we first applied MESSI to deimmunize a luciferase and a de novo designed mini-binder against PD-1, resulting in variants with no predicted epitopes and higher activity than their parents. Lastly, we coupled MESSI with evolution guidance to deimmunize uricase, a clinically approved enzyme with severe immunogenicity, and found deimmunized variants with higher catalytic activity than their natural orthologs. MESSI enables generative design of functional proteins with minimized immunogenicity, potentially making protein therapeutics safer and more effective.

items.abstract: Rare diseases can remain undiagnosed for years because individual disorders are uncom-mon and clinically heterogeneous, while relevant clues are distributed across structuredphenotypes, facial appearance, prior cases and disease knowledge. Computational toolscan use Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)-encoded findings, genomic data and increas-ingly diverse medical images, but these modalities are processed by models with differentoutputs and score scales. ZebraSeek converts clinical and facial inputs into ranked diseasecandidates with specialist tools, then uses a large language model (LLM) to integrateand externally check those candidates while retaining their sources. Facial-image analysisprovides a complementary machine-readable phenotype that can capture patterns notfully represented by manually encoded HPO terms. In 74 literature-derived cases spanning19 diseases, ZebraSeek placed the recorded diagnosis first in 50 (67.6%) and within fivein 59 (79.7%); it recovered 11 diagnoses outside PubCaseFinder’s top five, while fivediagnoses present in PubCaseFinder’s top five were absent from ZebraSeek’s final top five.During DBCLS BioHackathon 2026, we expanded analysis to 368 patients, 462 imagesand 54 disorders to examine how candidate depth affects coverage and downstreamcandidate count, and to assess the feasibility of case-specific candidate selection.

items.abstract: Abstract The growing volume and complexity of heterogeneous medical data create challenges in extracting diagnostic knowledge while preserving privacy because centralized models face high computation costs and security risks. To overcome this limitation, the novel Asynchronous Federated Multi-Convolution Spatial and Efficient Squeeze-Excitation Network (AFL-MCSESEN) with Bulyan-Based Adaptive Differential Privacy (BADP) was proposed for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Modal Data Fusion in Sustainable AI-Driven Healthcare Systems (HS) (AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS). Initially, Multi-modal data such as structured, semi-structured, and unstructured Knee Osteoarthritis data are collected and stored in Apache Spark managed by data lake. These heterogeneous sources are integrated using the Unified Element Tree Fusion method. Then, these fused data are processed through Z-score normalization and feature vector encoding. Simultaneously, the knee joint images are standardized for attaining consistent visual representation of pathological changes. Then, these pre-processed inputs are processed for Local Feature Extraction and Refinement using a Multi-Convolution Spatial and Efficient Squeeze-Excitation Network. Here, ResNet-34 backbone integrated with a Condensed Depthwise Squeeze-Excitation (CDSE) module and Multi-Convolution Spatial Attention (MCSA) was utilized to isolate subtle clinical indicators. To maintain institutional privacy, these features are trained within an privacy-preserving asynchronous federated learning framework, where ten institutional clients compute local gradients on vertically partitioned data using secure inner-product evaluations. Finally, a Bulyan-Based Adaptive Differential Privacy mechanism is utilized for further enhancing robustness and privacy. By this, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system provide sustainable, high-accuracy diagnostic tool for classifying Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) Grades of Knee Osteoarthritis such as Grade 0 (Healthy), Grade 1 (Doubtful), Grade 2 (Mild), Grade 3 (Moderate) and Grade 4 (Severe). Here, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system attains an Accuracy of 99.64%, an Area Under curve value as 0.998, Communication Overhead as 285MB, Data Integration Latency as 703.33ms, Spark Query Throughput as 516.67QPS, Attack Success Rate as 1.8 and Privacy-Utility Index (PUTI) as 0.96. By this results, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system provides the promising solution for Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Systems.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Dental calculus is a primary etiological factor in periodontal disease, disproportionately affecting underserved populations with limited access to professional dental care. Automated photographic oral disease screening tools may help bridge this access gap by enabling early identification of calculus burden in community, school-based, and remote settings. Methods A ResNet-50 encoder integrated within a U-Net segmentation architecture was trained on intraoral photographic images sourced from a public dataset. The dataset was partitioned into training (1,361 images; 66.5%), validation (584 images; 28.5%), and an independent held-out test set (103 images; 5.0%), with the test set withheld from all model development decisions. Manual polygon segmentation masks were created using CVAT. A pixel-area calculation technique was developed to estimate the percentage of tooth surface covered by calculus. Architecture comparisons were conducted against a standard U-Net (no pretraining), VGG16/U-Net, and EfficientNet-B4/U-Net under identical training conditions. Results On the held-out test set, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.731 (95% CI: 0.706–0.756), IoU of 0.698 (95% CI: 0.671–0.724), recall of 0.714, and specificity of 0.971. The pixel-level ROC-AUC was 0.931 (95% CI: 0.918–0.944) however, this value is inflated by background pixel dominance and should be interpreted alongside Dice and IoU as primary segmentation metrics. The proposed architecture outperformed all three comparators. Validation-set metrics (Dice 0.743, IoU 0.712) were modestly higher than test-set values, as expected given reduced optimization bias on unseen data. Conclusions This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that deep learning can support automated dental calculus screening from photographic images. Findings are preliminary and subject to important limitations including non-clinician annotation and a single public dataset source. With further clinical validation, such tools may contribute to scalable oral health monitoring in tele-dentistry workflows, school dental programs, and community health initiatives.

items.abstract: Abstract This study proposes a Foundation Artificial Intelligence (Foundation AI)-based multimodal human–machine interaction framework for an intelligent accelerometer-assisted robotic hand glove to support personalized upper-limb rehabilitation in Parkinson's disease patients. Approximately 150 participants (120 Parkinson's disease patients with Hoehn and Yahr Stage II–III and 30 healthy elderly volunteers) perform six clinically relevant Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), including grasping, eating, drinking, writing, dressing, and opening doors, to capture realistic neuromuscular movement patterns. The lightweight soft robotic glove integrates surface EMG sensors, an IMU incorporating a three-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, flex sensors, force-sensitive resistors, pressure sensors, vibration sensors, and temperature sensors to continuously monitor muscle activity, hand kinematics, tremor characteristics, grip force, wrist orientation, and movement acceleration. The embedded accelerometer enhances movement intention recognition by detecting motion direction, velocity, posture transitions, and dynamic hand activities. To improve accessibility, the framework incorporates three intelligent human–machine interaction modules: voice command control using Whisper and a Bidirectional Transformer for speech-driven robotic assistance; vision-based control via an external webcam, employing MediaPipe Hands for real-time hand landmark detection and Vision Transformer (ViT) for gesture recognition and movement intention estimation; and a mobile healthcare platform supporting personalized rehabilitation, remote monitoring, and secure telemedicine communication through Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), MQTT, and AES-256 encryption. The visual features extracted from the webcam are fused with multimodal physiological and motion signals through a Multimodal Foundation Transformer (MFT) incorporating cross-modal attention and self-supervised contrastive learning to estimate movement intention, tremor severity, hand gesture, finger trajectory, grasp type, and grip force. An Adaptive Impedance Controller subsequently personalizes robotic assistance by regulating actuator torque, finger motion, and wrist orientation in real time while continuously adapting to patient-specific neuromuscular conditions. The proposed framework establishes an intelligent multimodal perception and control architecture for personalized robotic rehabilitation and provides the computational foundation for future Digital Twin-enabled adaptive neuro-rehabilitation.

items.abstract: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

items.abstract: Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops. Our system, HexaShell, keeps the harness thin: it only turns the agent's commands into robot motion. The agent drives a robot with two arms through one command line. It sees three RGB cameras and knows their calibration. After each failed attempt, the agent reads the log, finds the cause, and writes or fixes small programs called tools. In this way it keeps what it learns as code, as a coding agent does when it fixes a failing test. The tools may use only what the robot observes. They use triangulation to find where objects are, relative to each other and to the gripper. If two cameras see the same point, the point lies where the two camera rays meet. If a point lies on a known plane, such as the table or the top of a block, it lies where its ray meets that plane. When the head camera is not enough, the robot moves a wrist camera to get a second view. We build the tools on only ten layouts of one seed per task, then freeze them and test them on ten new layouts of the same seed. We use Codex with GPT-6-Astra at medium reasoning effort. On all 42 RoboDojo tasks, HexaShell reaches a success rate of 39.7% and a progress score of 48.0, averaged in the same way as the leaderboard. This is a new state of the art on RoboDojo. The limit is contact, not reasoning: pushing reaches 92.5% and memory tasks 65.0%, but tight insertion only 8.3%. When the agent fails, it usually sees the failure but cannot make the motion work. We open source the tools evolved so far at https://github.com/HexaFuture/HexaShell.

items.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
items.summary: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to…
items.abstract: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. DLite directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model and performs local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining the historical context, transforming an increasingly complex modeling problem into local simple prediction problem. A lightweight sequential head further restores intra-block causal dependencies with low overhead. To effectively train this heterogeneous history-free architecture, we introduce a tailored two-stage training strategy. Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2-6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.

items.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
items.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is…
items.abstract: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.

items.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
items.summary: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives…
items.abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

items.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the…
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic-free, tree-aware posterior self-distillation framework for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn-level credit. It then maps each credit to a closed-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini-batches. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.

items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our…
items.abstract: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

items.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
items.summary: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not. In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to…
items.abstract: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not. In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list. We formalize open-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural-language reason why the item fits the needs of a decision maker. We propose QD-Rec, a quality--diversity method that selects items with a contextual bandit and generates hypotheses with a foundation model from earlier ones kept in an archive as stepping stones. A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor. Across M&A, customer targeting, and paper and book recommendation, QD-Rec gives the highest mean quality and builds the largest archive in most settings.

items.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
items.summary: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an…
items.abstract: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction. Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries. Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1. Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions. Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks. These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.

items.title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
items.summary: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS…
items.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.

items.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy…
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness. In light of this, we propose Self-HPO, a recursive self-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates (H-step). The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning (RL) under the selected harness (P-step), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy's evolving failure modes. Across three coding benchmarks, Self-HPO consistently outperforms harness-only and policy-only baselines, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%, with gains generalizing to out-of-distribution settings. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains. Self-HPO also improves reliability (Pass@1) and expands the capability frontier (Pass@k) over the base agent. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model (e.g., Opus 4.8) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost.

items.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines…
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features with visual latents, the language model's mask-token states, so mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an additional segmentation encoder. Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the regions it visits during chain-of-thought. As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models. Moreover, it surpasses Qwen3.5 across all perception benchmarks. Homepage: https://seerray-lab.github.io/Xiaomi-Lens-0{this https URL}

items.title: MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing
items.summary: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing. However, constructing high-quality multi-turn training data remains challenging, as conventional sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across editing turns. To address this challenge, we introduce MTEdit,…
items.abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing. However, constructing high-quality multi-turn training data remains challenging, as conventional sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across editing turns. To address this challenge, we introduce MTEdit, a multi-turn image editing dataset built through a pipeline centered on packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation. By jointly generating multiple editing states within a unified visual context, this pipeline reduces visual-quality drift across turns. Covering both step-wise and context-aware editing scenarios, MTEdit comprises 500K multi-turn image editing trajectories, with up to 8 turns and an average of 5.38 turns per trajectory, making it one of the most extensive datasets for multi-turn image editing. We further introduce MTEdit-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both scenarios by assessing models' ability to follow editing instructions, maintain content consistency, resist visual-quality drift, and effectively use historical context across turns. Using MTEdit, we fine-tune Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal to obtain Qwen-Image-MTEdit. On MTEdit-Bench, we evaluate a broad range of closed-source and open-source image editing models, including Qwen-Image-MTEdit. Experimental results show that Qwen-Image-MTEdit achieves the best performance among the evaluated open-source models, demonstrating the effectiveness of MTEdit in improving models' multi-turn image editing capabilities.

items.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
items.summary: Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design…
items.abstract: Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences. We construct two datasets: Scene-OTA-35K, which provides Observation--Thought--Action supervision for learning scene design and efficient error correction, and Scene-OTC-15K, which provides Observation--Thought--Critic supervision for learning scene quality critique across physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence. Based on these experiences, we propose Scene-GRPO, a Critic-guided GRPO framework that improves design decisions and reduces unnecessary trial-and-error corrections. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Scene-Designer achieves superior performance in physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence, while the learned Scene-Critic significantly outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique. Moreover, test-time Critic guidance further improves scene generation, showing that the Critic can provide useful guidance beyond training. Additional analysis suggests a trend of mutual enhancement between scene design and critique abilities.

items.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
items.summary: Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself. Yet benchmarks for this task in the context of visual coding remain scarce: existing resources are small and annotated only with layout boxes, so evaluation must fall back on VLM-as-judge…
items.abstract: Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself. Yet benchmarks for this task in the context of visual coding remain scarce: existing resources are small and annotated only with layout boxes, so evaluation must fall back on VLM-as-judge or human checklists rather than objective render-and-compare, and the generation methods they support design layouts from scratch, leaving human-crafted posters unusable as either a retrievable design library or as verified supervision. We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task. RAP contains 25K+ verified paper-poster pairs from various machine learning conferences held between 2022 and 2026, annotated with a three-level content taxonomy, plus a held-out benchmark of 150 test papers each paired with its human poster. A fully automated derendering pipeline turns each poster into styled HTML/CSS of typed, refillable slots, so every sample is a paper-poster-markup triplet verifiable by rendering against the source poster. The corpus serves both inference and training: PosterRAG, a training-free multi-agent pipeline, retrieves an exemplar and refills its slots without touching layout or styling, while an SFT+RL recipe trains a dedicated model from the same triplets. An online demo is available at https://reconstruct-a-poster.github.io/.

items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
items.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and…
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

items.title: Do People Still Matter? Healthcare in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms are becoming increasingly prevalent in healthcare. Unlike previous technologies, AI has the capability to perform tasks previously considered uniquely human including synthesizing historical information and data to establish a clinical diagnosis and constructing a treatment plan. AI promises to improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery and development, and enhance…
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms are becoming increasingly prevalent in healthcare. Unlike previous technologies, AI has the capability to perform tasks previously considered uniquely human including synthesizing historical information and data to establish a clinical diagnosis and constructing a treatment plan. AI promises to improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery and development, and enhance access to healthcare. The overall impact that AI will have on the well-being of individuals who provide and receive care, however, is less obvious. This article examines the potential and pitfalls of AI in medicine through the lens of mattering and its importance to human flourishing. Mattering is a psychological construct that encompasses the human needs to be noticed, feel significant, and contribute. It arises from interpersonal interactions and is based on perceptions of our value within our communities and society. Mattering is inherently relational, is a significant contributor to psychological well-being, and may be at risk in the age of AI. The authors describe the foundations of mattering and its relevance to medicine; the potential impacts of AI on mattering in medicine from the clinician, patient, and trainee perspectives; and propose a framework for integrating AI into healthcare such that mattering is preserved for all stakeholders.

items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) poses a serious global health threat, undermining treatment outcomes and necessitating the development of innovative therapeutic strategies. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a major contributor to this burden, with increasing prevalence in hospitals, contaminated food, and environmental sources. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic further intensified S. aureus resistance due to widespread antibiotic misuse. Biofilm formation, which facilitates the horizontal transfer of resistance genes such as mecA (methicillin resistance gene A), plays a central role in the development of resistance. To counteract antibiotic-resistant S. aureus , alternative approaches have emerged, including antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), photodynamic therapy (PDT), and drug repurposing guided by artificial intelligence (AI). Cutting-edge technologies such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-CRISPR-associated protein 13a (Cas13a)-based gene editing and engineered bacteriophages offer promising avenues for targeting resistant strains. Natural compounds such as thymol and chlorogenic acid (CGA) have also shown potential in reducing resistance and inhibiting biofilm formation. Effective management of AMR requires strengthened antibiotic stewardship programs (ASPs), robust surveillance systems, and public health measures such as proper hand hygiene and environmental sanitation. Combining antibiotic adjuvants (AAs) with existing antibiotics and leveraging bioactive peptides (BAPs) can enhance antibiotic efficacy against multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pan-drug-resistant (PDR) S. aureus . This review investigates the prevalence and resistance mechanisms of S. aureus in clinical, food, and environmental contexts, explores promising alternative therapies, and emphasizes the urgent need for global antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and sustainable intervention strategies.

items.abstract: Rare diseases represent a major unmet medical need, yet the development of therapeutics for these diseases is limited by small patient cohorts, fragmented data, and uncertain disease mechanisms. Recent advances that combine patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models with multi-omics profiling and artificial intelligence offer a robust approach for phenotype definition and drug target identification that requires only minimal patient material. By integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, machine learning can produce disease-relevant molecular signatures, identify convergent pathway drivers, and prioritize druggable targets despite limited sample sizes. This short review highlights emerging in vitro models and AI-enabled workflows, discusses their strengths and limitations, and outlines practical strategies to accelerate drug discovery for rare diseases.

items.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) inhibitors are considered promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer and several other diseases. In this study, regression QSAR models for HDAC8 inhibitors were developed using various types of molecular descriptors and machine learning algorithms. The best-performing weighted consensus model achieved an external predictive performance of Q 2 test = 0.62 for the complete test set and 0.71 for compounds within the applicability domain, covering 77% of the external data. Model reliability was confirmed by five-fold cross-validation and y-randomization tests. The developed QSAR model was integrated into the HDAC8 Assistant web application (https://hdac8-assistant.streamlit.app/), which includes a de novo molecular generation module based on recurrent neural networks (SMILES-RNN) and reinforcement learning (REINVENT 2). For targeted discovery of novel inhibitors, an original reward function was proposed that combines QSAR-predicted activity with applicability domain control for generated compounds. This approach enables simultaneous optimization of predicted inhibitory activity while limiting extrapolation beyond the model applicability domain. HDAC8 Assistant also implements assessment of drug-likeness according to the Muegge criteria, as well as PAINS, toxicophore, and Brenk structural-alert detection. Molecular docking was performed for the most promising compounds generated by HDAC8 Assistant to analyse their interactions with the HDAC8 active site.

items.abstract: Machine learning models for molecular discovery often train on bioactivity data from heterogeneous assays, yet assay context is rarely explicitly represented. We investigate whether natural-language assay descriptions provide predictive information beyond molecular and protein representations. We develop ACL-DTI (Assay-aware Contrastive Learning-based Drug Target Interaction) and MAMMAL-AsAP, an assay-context extension of MAMMAL-DTI. Across five triplet-disjoint random splits, assay-aware models achieve competitive or improved performance over assay-agnostic baselines. Among the evaluated models, MAMMAL-AsAP achieves the highest (R^2) of 0.7198 +/- 0.0085. Masking experiments show that ACL-DTI is robust to incomplete assay descriptions, exhibiting the smallest reductions in R^2 among the evaluated models when masking the target name, assay technique, or both: 0.0228 +/- 0.0064, 0.0406 +/- 0.0113, and 0.0620 +/- 0.0190, respectively. These results indicate that assay descriptions contain predictive information not fully captured by molecular structures and protein sequences, and reveal architecture-dependent differences in how this information is exploited.

items.abstract: The clinical implementation of precision oncology remains challenged by intratumoral heterogeneity, complex tumor microenvironment interactions, and the limited predictive value of conventional preclinical models. 3D cancer spheroids have emerged as physiologically relevant platforms that closely mimic in vivo tumor architecture, cellular heterogeneity, hypoxic gradients, and treatment resistance mechanisms. This review highlights the growing role of cancer spheroids in drug panel testing and their application in personalized therapeutic decision-making across diverse malignancies, including breast, colorectal, ovarian, lung, head and neck, and brain cancers. Patient-derived spheroids and multicellular co-culture models preserve critical tumor-stroma and tumor-immune interactions, enabling clinically meaningful evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents, targeted therapies, immunotherapies, radiosensitizers, and combination treatment strategies. Drug panels assessed using spheroid platforms encompass platinum-based agents, EGFR and VEGF inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, kinase inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and emerging pathway-directed therapeutics. Accumulating evidence suggests that spheroid-based drug testing has the potential to recapitulate clinically relevant tumor characteristics and treatment responses and may serve as a useful preclinical approach for evaluating drug sensitivity, exploring resistance mechanisms, and assessing biomarker-associated responses within clinically relevant timeframes. Recent advances in high-throughput screening, microfluidic technologies, organ-on-chip systems, automated imaging, and artificial intelligence-driven analytics have further improved the scalability, reproducibility, and translational utility of these models. The review also discusses the current limitations, standardization challenges, and ethical considerations associated with spheroid-based drug testing. Collectively, personalized cancer spheroids represent a promising approach linking experimental oncology with precision medicine research, with potential applications in individualized drug testing and treatment optimization.

items.abstract: Comparative studies increasingly score amino-acid variation across species with structure-based predictors applied to a single structural template, but whether the template itself can create associations with species traits has received little attention. We examined this while testing whether long-lived species carry proteins predicted to be more stable or, under nearly neutral theory, less stable. In two independent tetrapod radiations, 57 placental mammals (1,755 genes) and 40 reptiles and amphibians (1,910 genes), we reconstructed ancestral proteins, predicted with ThermoMPNN the folding effect of every amino-acid difference between the ancestor and each species on AlphaFold backbones, and related the mean effect to lifespan by phylogenetic regression, following analysis plans fixed in advance. With a human backbone, primates, which are long-lived for their size, appeared least destabilized, producing a weak apparent association with lifespan. In a pre-specified confirmatory test, a platypus backbone reduced the primate offset from -1.96 to -0.62 SD and the association disappeared (P = 0.701). In reptiles, a human backbone, although equidistant in time, favoured slowly evolving turtles and crocodilians and gave a nominal association that two fish backbones did not reproduce. The predictor captured site-level stability signal, yet with outgroup templates neither radiation showed a robust association between predicted stability and longevity, although moderate effects cannot be excluded. The choice of structural template can therefore create apparent cross-species associations. We propose four checks to detect them: ancestral references, outgroup templates, tests for clade and rate effects, and tests of dependence on a few clades.

items.abstract: In recent years, deep learning has revolutionized protein structure prediction, achieving remarkable speed and accuracy. RNA structure prediction, however, has lagged behind. Although several methods have shown moderate success in predicting RNA secondary and tertiary structures, none have reached the accuracy observed with contemporary protein models. The lack of success of these RNA structure prediction models has been proposed to be due to limited high-quality structural information that can be used as training data. To probe this proposed limitation, we developed a large and diverse data set comprising paired RNA sequences and their corresponding secondary structures. We assessed the utility of this enhanced data set by retraining a deep-learning model, SincFold. We find that SincFold exhibited improved performance on a set of previously unseen RNA families, enhancing its capability to predict accurate de novo RNA secondary structures. We additionally implemented Lyra-TransPred, which achieved the highest mean F1 and MCC among the evaluated models while requiring substantially less training time per epoch. The RNASSTR data set provides a substantial advance for RNA structure modeling, laying a strong foundation for the development of future RNA secondary structure prediction algorithms.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

items.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.

items.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by long-term and dynamic interactions between the immune system and pancreatic β-cells, ultimately leading to severe insulin deficiency. A paradigm shift in T1DM research has occurred in the past few years, with research now focusing on the human disease because of access to human pancreatic tissue and pancreas-draining lymph nodes. Advances in high-resolution imaging, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and histopathology based on artificial intelligence have profoundly reshaped our understanding of disease initiation and progression. These studies revealed that β-cell loss and/or dysfunction might begin earlier than previously appreciated, preferentially affecting small β-cell-rich islets and insulin-positive cell clusters, with larger islets showing transient resistance. Substantial β-cell mass often persists at diagnosis, accompanied by functional impairment rather than immediate cell death. Across disease stages, β-cells exhibit conserved molecular signatures dominated by interferon signalling, enhanced antigen presentation and adaptive immune-evasion programmes, with evidence of heterogeneity linked to age, disease duration and immune context. Parallel analyses of pancreatic lymph nodes show early immune dysregulation, including altered regulatory T cell signatures and expansion of stem-like cytotoxic T cell populations, even before overt hyperglycaemia. Together, these findings support an integrated model of T1DM progression that enables alignment of clinical staging with evolving β-cell and immune phenotypes.

items.abstract: Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors. In this paper we show that these residuals contain structured biological information. We introduce and validate a conditional discordance framework that uses foundation model prediction residuals to identify tissue regions where morphology and transcriptome diverge. The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients. In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients. In two sections of P07, discordant regions enriched in tumor cells showed greater underprediction of transcription associated with EMT after composition adjustment, without a robust increase in observed program expression. Gene predictability is associated with spatial autocorrelation. Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathway profiles were more similar within patients, although the permutation test allowed only nine assignments (p=1/9). Application to four colorectal specimens supported broader use of the framework. The framework shows that prediction residuals carry biological information about microenvironmental heterogeneity, without identifying a universal EMT state.

items.abstract: End-to-end visual generation with pixel-space loss has recently achieved competitive performance without the need for learned image tokenizers. In this work, we study whether language-informed supervision can provide a richer training signal than pixel loss for visual generation. We introduce LILIE (pronounced "lily"), a Language-Informed and Lossless Image Encoder. LILIE is an invertible image transform trained such that a vision-language model can recover captions from noised features. The encoder uses a normalizing flow transformer trained jointly with a vision-language model via next token prediction. We then use the encoder to extract a simple language-informed loss for text-to-image generation. We train JiT models with LILIE loss, reducing gFD by 14 points (66.84 to 53.01) against a pixel-only baseline on the GPIC dataset. Our code, encoders, and generative models are available at https://suchiragarwal.com/lilie.

items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.

items.abstract: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records. CP's two-bit code lowers output KL by 41--63\% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest. Analysis across three trained n-gram memory families shows that Gaussian-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low-rank residual variants we test. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.

items.abstract: Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) depends on unsafe multimodal data for post-training alignment or activation steering. However, such data is hard to collect, must be gathered anew for each modality, and its collection and distribution raise ethical and legal concerns. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a lightweight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility up to over-refusal. MARS reveals that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.

items.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt

items.abstract: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens. Consider two different prompts followed by the same continuation text, so that any difference in their hidden states comes from the prompt alone, and we find that the distance between their hidden states decays approximately as a power law t^{-α}, where α=1 is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks and smaller values mean longer memory. Trained models forget fast (αapprox0.55--0.7), untrained ones slowly (αapprox0.2--0.5). We prove that this offset is Obig(P(log t)^{L-1}/tbig) for a prompt of length P and depth L. The bound holds for finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits, under one additional condition: the pre-norm activations stay away from zero. The mechanism is geometric: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and relay --- continuation tokens passing on what earlier tokens read from the prompt --- can only add logarithmic factors. This is what we call the conditional no-hair theorem: given the text generated so far, the prompt's influence on the next token vanishes as t grows, so any property of the prompt that survives, such as its language, must be carried by the text itself. An exactly solvable linear relay model shows that the bound cannot be improved and reproduces the rise of the local exponent towards 1 seen in untrained networks. Cancelling the dilution with a logit bias stops the decay early in training and reverses it after, so dilution is necessary for the forgetting we measure; untrained networks and the solvable model show it is also sufficient.

items.summary: Language models are increasingly trained against several verifiable rewards at once, such as the correctness and the format of a tool call, or the individual constraints of a complex instruction. items.abstract: Language models are increasingly trained against several verifiable rewards at once, such as the correctness and the format of a tool call, or the individual constraints of a complex instruction. Reward-decoupled normalization (GDPO) normalizes each reward separately so that different reward combinations keep distinct advantages, but it still spreads every reward's advantage evenly over the whole response, although each verifier checks only a few positions. We propose MRTPO, which assigns the advantage of each reward to the tokens relevant to it, using the information its verifier checks, without auxiliary models or token-level annotations. For each reward, the policy replays its own response with and without that reward's verifier information, and the per-token Jensen-Shannon distance between the two next-token distributions measures each token's relevance and reassigns the advantage. On text-to-SQL, multi-constraint instruction following and tool calling, MRTPO converges faster and achieves better performance than the compared methods.

items.summary: Large language model agents solve tasks through long sequences of tool calls, and the prevailing design has a single strong model generate every step, although many steps are routine enough for a much smaller model. items.abstract: Large language model agents solve tasks through long sequences of tool calls, and the prevailing design has a single strong model generate every step, although many steps are routine enough for a much smaller model. Existing ways of sharing this work keep the strong model as the generator: routers and collaborative agents decide which model handles each query or step, and speculative methods check a small model's drafts one step at a time, usually against the strong model's own action. We introduce SpecAgent, a collaboration protocol that turns the strong model from the author of each step into a reviewer of steps drafted by a weak model. The weak model executes read-only tool calls as it drafts, so that every step is grounded in real observations, and holds the first action that would modify the environment. The strong model then verifies the drafted segment in a single prefill pass, commits the longest prefix it judges semantically valid, and repairs the first rejected step. Because verification replaces autoregressive decoding with parallel prefill, the strong model decodes only short verdicts and occasional repairs rather than every step. On τ^2-Bench, SpecAgent comes within one point of the strong model's success rate while roughly halving memory traffic and wall time, and on AutomationBench and VitaBench it recovers 44-75% of the quality gap while lowering both. In an edge-cloud deployment on MCP-Atlas with three cloud models, it closes 53-75% of the weak-strong quality gap while the strong model generates at most half as many tokens. These results suggest that a strong model need not author every step of an agent: reviewing grounded drafts retains most of its quality while cutting both latency and memory traffic.

items.abstract: Recent advances in Omni Language Models (OLMs) provide a unified solution for audiovisual video captioning. Nevertheless, existing approaches predominantly treat captioning as an unstructured text generation process, neglecting the inherent semantic structure of videos and leading to suboptimal fine-grained audiovisual alignment. To bridge this gap, we propose EVA-Cap, a novel framework that decomposes captions into atomic audiovisual events and transforms unstructured text supervision into event-centric alignment. We train EVA-Cap via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on a self-curated dataset, EVA-Data, which is built with event-centric quality control. During the GRPO phase, the model is explicitly optimized against three event-centric alignment targets: global event completeness, intra-event attribution, and inter-event synchronization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EVA-Cap significantly outperforms existing methods in event-centric evaluation (e.g., +9.0% average gain on ChronusAV), while achieving competitive performance on general audiovisual captioning benchmarks (e.g., +3.3% on WorldSense).
