items.abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 30%–40% of patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC) develop local recurrence or distant metastasis. Early identification of high-risk patients is therefore important for improving prognosis. Methods A total of 1,285 patients with LANPC from three medical centers were enrolled. Patients from center A were randomly divided into a training set (n = 693) and a validation set (n = 297) at a ratio of 7:3, while patients from centers B and C were combined as an external test set (n = 295). Ten independent machine learning models and 26 stacked ensemble models were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. The incremental value of multidimensional habitat (MH) features over clinical features alone was assessed using integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to interpret the final model. Results After recursive feature elimination (RFE), four selected clinical features, namely N category, treatment, platelet count (PLT), and smoking status, were identified and further combined with two imaging features, namely multidimensional habitats derived from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1C MH) and multidimensional habitats derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI MH), for model development. The stacked ensemble model combining support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and logistic regression (LR) achieved the best overall performance, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.761 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.719–0.798) in the 5-fold cross-validation set, 0.742 (95% CI: 0.679–0.801) in the validation set, and 0.721 (95% CI: 0.660–0.776) in the external test set. Conclusion In conclusion, the stacking model constructed based on SVM, GBM, and LR, integrating MH features and clinical features, demonstrated favorable predictive performance for recurrence and metastasis in LANPC patients, and holds promise as an effective tool for individualized risk assessment. Evidence Level: 3 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2

items.abstract: Background: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is an important MRI technique for studying tissue microstructure and structural connectivity, but is limited by relatively low spatial resolution, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and sensitivity to inter-acquisition motion. A deep-learning framework was developed that jointly performs image registration and super-resolution on repeated low-resolution DWI inputs to generate a single registered, higher apparent spatial-resolution output. Methods: DeepSUM-DWI adapts a DeepSUM multi-image super-resolution architecture for repeated DWI. It comprises a shared 2D super-resolution feature extractor (SISRNet), a registration network (RegNet), and a 3D fusion network (FusionNet). Evaluation used (1) simulated repetitions with synthetic motion, (2) retrospectively downsampled acquisitions from 12 subjects, and (3) a prospective dual-resolution example with matched 1.0 × 1.0 and 2.0 × 2.0 mm² acquisitions. Results: DeepSUM-DWI reconstructed a single high-resolution-appearing DWI image from multiple low-resolution repetitions while preserving structural characteristics of the high-resolution acquisitions. The model remained robust across synthetic motion magnitudes. In retrospectively downsampled data, it improved NRMSE by 71–79% and PSNR by 10.6–13.5 dB, for super-resolution factors of 2–3, relative to averaging interpolated low-resolution images, with a mean SSIM > 0.99. In prospectively acquired data, it recovered finer structures than visible in the acquired low-resolution images while maintaining contrast consistency. Exploratory diffusion analysis suggested that some gains in apparent detail propagated to FA maps. Conclusions: DeepSUM-DWI provides a framework for joint registration and super-resolution of repeated DWI acquisitions, with potential to improve apparent spatial resolution while retaining the SNR benefits of repeated acquisition.

items.abstract: Using an analysis pipeline that combines machine learning-based feature selection with classical statistical modelling, we aimed to predict incident inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and to identify candidate proteins associated with disease development. We used UK Biobank data in an observational cohort study of 52,331 participants with proteomics data and without a history of IBD. The cohort was split into an 80/20 train/test dataset, and three separate extreme gradient boosting models were trained on the training dataset. Using Shapley values, we ranked the predictive importance of 2,912 proteins for incident IBD, Crohn's disease (CD), and ulcerative colitis (UC). The top 20 proteins per outcome served as features in multivariate Cox models predicting 350 incident cases over 14 years. All three proteomics Cox models showed moderate discrimination in the test dataset, with the UC model performing the best (C-index: 0.68), followed by IBD (C-index: 0.65), and CD (C-index: 0.60). All proteomics models outperformed clinical models. Smoking remained the only significant clinical predictor in the combined proteomics + clinical model. 48 unique proteins were identified across the three models, with 16 reaching statistical significance (p< 0.05). Machine learning-based feature selection with statistical survival modelling identifies plasma proteins that predict incident IBD and highlight biologically plausible, potentially targetable pathways in the preclinical phase of IBD.

items.abstract: Tumour heterogeneity reflects both cellular identity (lineage) and state (active transcriptional programs), yet computational methods generally analyse these axes separately. We introduce CellScribe, a generative framework that conditions a pretrained language model on frozen single cell foundation model embeddings through AdaLN adapters, enabling one shared model to generate an ontology- grounded cell type or a quantified meta-program profile. Supervised multitask fine- tuning produces fine grained typing across hundreds of cell types and outperforms generative and retrieval baselines on meta-program identification under study-holdout evaluation. We further train the model with reinforcement learning, scoring its generations against cell ontology distance and meta-program agreement, so that they align with biological knowledge rather than token agreement. To identify new cell types not present in the supervised training data, we post-train the model to read several labelled example cells in a single context, each conditioning its own text span, and infer the type of a query cell through in-context learning. CellScribe thus unifies cell identity and state in one generative interface, grounds both in biological structure, and identifies cell types outside the supervised vocabulary.

items.abstract: Pancreatic lipomatosis, characterized by progressive adipose replacement of the exocrine pancreas, is a known consequence of chronic pancreatitis. Despite its clinical relevance, the mechanisms driving lipomatosis remain poorly understood. Here, we used a pancreas-specific NF-κB-inducing kinase (NIK) stabilization mouse model to investigate how sustained non-canonical NF-κB signaling contributes to chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic lipomatosis. NIK stabilization initiated a rapid and fully penetrant pancreatic remodeling program, leading to acinar cell death already by the end of the first week of age. Deep learning on high-definition spatial transcriptomics revealed a progressive loss of acinar identity resulting in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation and identified GPA33 as a novel surface marker of ADMs. Over time, ADM lesions underwent apoptosis, leading to progressive loss of pancreatic parenchyma, organ atrophy, and extensive adipose replacement. Mechanistically, Relb deletion fully rescued the NIK-induced pancreatic phenotype, demonstrating that chronic pancreatitis and lipomatosis require RelB-dependent non-canonical NF-κB signaling in this model. Together, these findings define a RelB-dependent pathway linking sustained NIK stabilization to chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic lipomatosis. Our study provides a model for studying the development of pancreatic lipomatosis and for exploring potential therapeutic approaches.

items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. items.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average 3.16times decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) hold broad knowledge in one set of weights, but lack interpretability and trustworthy reasoning, especially in high-stakes use cases. A neuro-symbolic model, with its interpretable architecture and System 2 reasoning capacity, is a promising alternative if built at the scale of LLMs; however, its symbolic backbone is usually constructed with human effort, so existing neuro-symbolic models are bottlenecked by the scope of the symbol component and usually domain-specific. A data-driven method could instead build a larger symbolic system by aligning and merging existing ones. We target its first, foundational step: matching units across these heterogeneous systems. Our method, SAE-IDF, encodes a symbol in its native context into a sparse code with a sparse autoencoder (SAE), re-weights each dimension by its rarity and matches across systems. On 12 tasks across 6 kinds of symbolic system, SAE-IDF outperforms the same LLM's dense baseline on all tasks with Gemma-2-9B and all but one with Llama-3.1-8B, by up to 45 points, consistently across SAE layers and configurations. SAE-IDF is also interpretable: every dimension of the sparse code has a human-readable meaning, so each match decomposes into named concepts (features). Our work paves the way to a universal symbolic backbone.

items.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
items.summary: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediate execution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where…
items.abstract: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediate execution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where intermediate violations can incur financial losses or regulatory consequences regardless of the final outcome. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce BizBench, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in real-world procedures from a leading payments company. Its executable environment integrates 789 knowledge documents and 601 discoverable business tools, with consistent policies, states, and tool behavior. The benchmark comprises 50 tasks involving resource constraints, temporal dependencies, prior commitments, and conflicting or outdated guidance. Each task is validated through reference execution, while deterministic checks assess both goal attainment and execution validity without prescribing a single solution path. Experiments reveal substantial limitations even among frontier models: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol achieve strict success rates of only 64.0% and 61.3%, respectively. For Qwen3.8-27B, goal attainment reaches 42.0%, but strict success drops to 32.7%, demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation can mask invalid execution. Beyond success rates, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash averages 191.3 tool calls per run, approximately 70% more than reference executions, revealing substantial execution overhead. Overall, BizBench establishes a testbed for evaluating and advancing long-horizon agents beyond task completion, toward reliable and constraint-compliant execution in complex business environments.

items.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. items.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

items.abstract: We seek a hierarchical resolution of residual error under a composite learning objective as a principled mechanism for identifying and exploiting additional information, particularly under distribution shift and perturbation. Inspired by the System 1/System 2 paradigm, we formulate this principle as a two-loop mechanism serving a common inference goal. A fast, System 1-like loop resolves the residual addressable by the available evidence; the remaining epistemic residual triggers a medium speed, System 2-like loop that actively acquires additional evidence and measures its informational value through residual reduction. Over nested solution spaces, the medium-loop optimum is provably no worse than the fast-loop optimum. Experiments show that the resulting two-loop model consistently improves upon the fast loop at approximately half the computation of the medium loop, including under unseen corruptions, and, when provided a cleaner observation, outperforms staged classifiers and learning-to-defer methods at equal computational cost.

items.title: Recognition Is Not Grounding: Benchmarking Multilingual Financial Evidence Extraction
items.summary: Comparing financial disclosures across languages requires identifying shared accounting concepts and recovering all numerical facts that express them. Existing benchmarks evaluate aspects of these capabilities, but provide limited insight into whether both succeed on the same multilingual evidence. In particular, it remains unclear whether language models can recognize these concepts across languages and…
items.abstract: Comparing financial disclosures across languages requires identifying shared accounting concepts and recovering all numerical facts that express them. Existing benchmarks evaluate aspects of these capabilities, but provide limited insight into whether both succeed on the same multilingual evidence. In particular, it remains unclear whether language models can recognize these concepts across languages and exhaustively recover their corresponding numerical evidence from the same contexts. We introduce MULTIFINGROUND, a benchmark designed to investigate this recognition-grounding gap in multilingual financial reports. Constructed from FY2025 disclosures of 90 issuers in English, French, and Greek, MULTIFINGROUND aligns independently authored reports through a shared accounting taxonomy and provides traceable fact-level annotations. The benchmark evaluates financial fact identification, concept recognition, exhaustive fact selection, and concept discrimination without candidate labels. Across 15 evaluated models, eight API and open-weight reference models achieve 97.3-99.4\% concept recognition accuracy, yet miss at least one target fact in 26.6-41.9\% of correctly recognized groups. Further analyses reveal substantial variation in concept discrimination and limited gains from the evaluated finance-specialized models. Our findings demonstrate that strong concept recognition can coexist with incomplete evidence recovery, highlighting the importance of evaluating semantic recognition and evidence completeness together.

items.abstract: Background The valorization of hemoglobin (Hb) from meat processing by-products is essential for sustainable recycling. However, this process is severely constrained by the inherent limitations of Hb, such as poor stability and low solubility. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a computationally guided dual-modification strategy. This approach integrates covalent phosphorylation with epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)-mediated non-covalent interactions to enhance the applicability of modified Hb. Results Artificial neural network prediction and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to rationalize the modification process. MD simulations and binding energy calculations revealed that the stability of the complex is driven by specific amino acid residues, with ALA142, ASN139 and THR38 making the most significant contributions through robust hydrogen bonding networks. Spectroscopic analysis confirmed that this interaction with EGCG drastically reduced the α-helix content (from 74% to 30%), inducing a conformational opening that exposed cryptic hydrophobic pockets. The modified Hb exhibited superior surface hydrophobicity, antioxidant activity and foaming capacity. Crucially, application in a pork meat sausage model demonstrated that the EGCG-phosphorylated porcine hemoglobin (EGCG-PHb) complex effectively acted, overcoming the severe gel brittleness caused by phosphorylation and significantly enhancing the springiness and chewiness of the meat matrix. Conclusion The protein structure of the EGCG-PHb complex was significantly altered compared to Hb, and EGCG-PHb complex also significantly improved the springiness and chewiness of pork sausages. This dual-modification strategy provides new insights into the development and utilization of Hb. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.abstract: Accurate prediction of large protein assembly structures is crucial for understanding biological processes, yet remains a challenge for end-to-end approaches such as AlphaFold owing to their large size and intricate multi-chain interactions. Docking methods can handle large proteins, but suffer from the huge combinatorial binding space of multiple chains. Assembly methods offer an alternative way, but critically rely on the quality of predicted subcomponents. Here we present HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), a framework that integrates docking and combinatorial assembly for structure prediction of large protein complexes. HDM efficiently reduces reliance on subcomponent quality through docking, while leveraging the pairwise interactions of subcomponents through assembly. When evaluated on 3 benchmarks of 35 large heteromeric complexes, 172 large protein complexes and 7 CASP15 targets, HDM substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods including CombFold, MoLPC, AlphaFold-Multimer and AlphaFold3. In addition, HDM also demonstrates the capacity to predict the stoichiometry and model the complex without stoichiometry input.

items.abstract: Conventional aptamer discovery by systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is often constrained by limited library capacity, PCR bias, and multi-round screening. The recent convergence of artificial intelligence with aptamer development is driving a paradigm shift from empirical screening toward rational, data-driven design. This Review presents a timely and comprehensive overview of AI integration across the entire aptamer development pipeline, with a particular emphasis on advances reported in 2024-2026. We begin by discussing bioinformatics databases and computational tools for high-throughput SELEX data analysis. We then review state-of-the-art strategies for secondary and tertiary structure prediction, including recent breakthroughs such as AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFoldNA, and diffusion-based approaches. We also cover machine learning methods for aptamer-target interaction prediction, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations. A major focus is placed on very recent AI-driven generative design, including diffusion models (AptaDiff), language model-based frameworks (InstructNA, GRAPE-LM), and reinforcement learning approaches (AiDTA) for de novo aptamer generation and optimization. Emerging applications of AI-designed aptamers in precision diagnostics, targeted therapy, and biosensing are also surveyed. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future directions toward closed-loop, interpretable AI frameworks for translational aptamer development. By synthesizing the latest computational and experimental advances, this Review aims to serve as a timely resource for researchers seeking to leverage AI for next-generation aptamer discovery.

items.abstract: Tocilizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-6 receptor, is widely used in immune-mediated diseases, yet its real-world safety in pediatric populations remains insufficiently characterized. This retrospective pharmacovigilance study analyzed adverse event (AE) reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (2010-2025), focusing on pediatric cases where tocilizumab was the primary suspect drug. After data cleaning, 1,485 reports were included. Four classical disproportionality methods - reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multiple gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS) - were used to identify safety signals. Time-to-onset, stratified, and Weibull analyses were applied to characterize adverse event patterns, and network pharmacology was used to explore potential underlying mechanisms. Females accounted for 58.9% of reports, and adolescents aged 12-17 years represented the largest group. A total of 109 safety signals were identified. The most frequently reported AEs included juvenile idiopathic arthritis (ROR = 28.62, 95% CI: 24.30-33.72), haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (ROR = 15.83, 95% CI: 13.18-19.02), and decreased white blood cell count (ROR = 12.14, 95% CI: 9.90-14.88). Potential unlisted AEs, such as sudden hearing loss (ROR = 48.11, 95% CI: 16.74-138.26) and psoriasis (ROR = 11.44, 95% CI: 8.81-14.85), were also detected. Most AEs occurred within 30 days, with a median onset of 14 days, and showed an early failure pattern. Network pharmacology suggested psoriasis may involve JAK-STAT and Th17/Th1 pathways, though further validation is needed. Overall, this study provides real-world evidence to support improved safety monitoring in pediatric patients.

items.abstract: MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. % To break this loop, in this paper, we propose Compressed Window Auto-Regression (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.

The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a…
items.abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. This allows us to correct predictions at intermediate denoising steps, preventing early artifacts from persisting into the final sample. Although the corrector is trained only on predictions from the base denoiser, it can be applied repeatedly to its own outputs at inference for better results. This simple framework leads to substantial improvement in sample quality while largely preserving diversity. We evaluate our method across DiT, SiT, and JiT. Our method substantially improves upon previously reported FID scores for unguided generation and, notably, unconditional generation, where producing high-quality samples without guidance has been particularly challenging. Our method achieves performance competitive with classifier-free guidance (CFG), and combining correction with CFG further improves diversity and reduces oversaturation typical of CFG. Finally, we show that the additional inference cost of correction can be amortized by distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model, retaining the quality gains without additional inference-time overhead.

items.abstract: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. As these models are increasingly used for automated decision-making, understanding their reliability under adversarial manipulation becomes critical. We introduce DecisionRobust, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of decision models across textual and visual inputs. Our benchmark covers practical decision-making scenarios and a diverse suite of attacks, including semantics-preserving text perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities. We curate evaluation sets through external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection. We evaluate 30 model configurations on text tasks and 17 on vision tasks, including 24 and 12 held-out models, respectively, that are excluded from candidate selection. Our experiments reveal several key findings. First, attacks expose vulnerabilities beyond the models used for construction and selection, although optimized image perturbations transfer weakly to many targets even with multiple surrogates. Second, relative model robustness varies across tasks and attack types, and resistance to input perturbations does not necessarily imply resistance to prompt injection. Third, label-consistency checks substantially reduce measured attack success across text and image settings, highlighting the importance of validating apparent failures. The benchmark is available at https://yifan-lan.github.io/DecisionRobust/.

items.abstract: AI agents are demonstrating increasingly strong offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities in the real world. Current benchmarks mostly evaluate agents in isolation against static targets. Real cyber operations, however, are dynamic and coupled: security postures constantly change as attackers and defenders adapt to each other in real time. Static benchmarks quickly saturate and miss an agent's ability to attack and defend simultaneously under live pressure. To address this gap, we present CyberArena, a dynamic, symmetric adversarial benchmark built around multi-round attack-and-defense combat. In isolated sandboxes, two agents compete under identical rules, acting concurrently as both attackers and defenders over continuously changing services. This converts static targets into evolving, semi-open challenges, directly testing an agent's speed and precision in discovering, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities. To sustain the benchmark's longevity, an automated agentic pipeline continuously generates, reviews, and validates new environments. Furthermore, because pairwise contests are notoriously hard to quantify, we introduce a dynamical model that maps match dynamics into unified, multidimensional scores across offensive, defensive, and domain-specific capabilities. Evaluating 12 frontier LLM agents across 40 challenges in 466 matches, CyberArena separates model capabilities where single-agent baselines hit a ceiling. The trajectories read like a fight rather than an exam: defenders patch one hole and miss the next and certify repairs on stale evidence, while capable agents think a move ahead, planting backdoors for later rounds and, in one case, writing their own packet sniffer to watch the opponent. Beyond a benchmark, CyberArena serves as an adaptable, scalable experimental platform for future research on cybersecurity agents.

items.abstract: Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects. Rather than treating compressed histories or reconstructed accounts of progress as the primary basis for continuation, CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions. A core challenge is keeping this reusable basis valid after its surrounding history is retired: how can CarryOn update the basis without reconstructing the full representation at every fold? CarryOn maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and applicable environment checks while carrying forward unaffected records and jointly updating execution context. Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus show improved gains of 5.8% and 7.0% while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%, respectively. Project page: https://ethannju.github.io/carryon

items.abstract: Evaluation for automatic crisis reporting should measure what practitioners need, not what is convenient to compare. Through LLM-assisted, author-approved content analysis, we derive a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports using qualitative content analysis, then evaluate 121 human and 261 LLM-generated reports across five disasters and three hazard types. Under google/gemini-3.7-flash on Cyclone Idai, the best machine arm is nominally above the empirical human ceiling (0.827 vs. 0.821), but the difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95\% bootstrap CI [-.049,.059]; permutation p=.852), and the ordering does not replicate under openai/gpt-5.6-luna. On a blind 100-item Idai sample, the author agrees with the Gemini judge at 0.910 accuracy and unweighted Cohen's κ=.799. All four judges clear the plan's raw-agreement criterion of .7; only Gemini reaches .7 on chance-corrected κ. Across the three primary events, machine reports reproduce 5.4-11.0% of same-day official figures. Across those same events, raw exact-number matching links 14.3-19.6% of official figures and 85.4-90.1% of machine figures to the social stream; manual audit confirms 45/50 declared absences, 4/25 official matches, and 24/25 machine matches semantically. The issuing-provenance gap is positive in all 12 observed event-judge cells: report date, organisation, series, and authority were not supplied at professional-report coverage in any cell. On the three primary events, ROUGE-L is uninformative, BERTScore is negatively associated with completeness after multiplicity correction, and a generic LLM judge changes sign.

items.abstract: Post-training is crucial for improving text-to-image models, yet existing pipelines typically rely on manually curated training data and fixed training distributions. We introduce APT (Agentic Post-Training), a fully automated framework that adaptively post-trains a base model according to its evolving capability profile. APT coordinates three agents to construct evaluation sets from user requirements, diagnose model-specific strengths and failure modes, and generate reinforcement learning data with an adaptive prompt distribution that emphasizes underperforming capabilities. By repeatedly evaluating, diagnosing, and updating the generator, APT lets the current model's behavior shape its next training tasks, forming a feedback loop inspired by recursive self-improvement. For general-purpose settings without user-specified evaluation scenarios, we further develop an evaluation harness that enables broad and diverse evaluation set generation. Experiments across multiple base models, benchmarks, and generation architectures demonstrate that APT is model-agnostic, benchmark-agnostic, architecture-agnostic, and fully automated.

items.abstract: We introduce LensErase, a general-purpose mask-based Erase Anything foundation model designed to cover a broad spectrum of real-world erase scenarios. LensErase supports diverse objects, visual text, watermarks, associated visual effects, multiple-object removal, and a wide range of object scales, aspect ratios, and image resolutions. First, to enable such broad coverage, we construct LensErase-100M, a large-scale dataset containing 101.07 million paired source-mask-target examples spanning diverse erase scenarios. Second, we pretrain LensErase from the text-to-image model Lens, adapting its strong generative prior to mask-based erasing. To efficiently incorporate the source image and erase mask, we propose Mask-Aware RoPE, a 3D rotary positional encoding that directly injects mask information into the source-image tokens without introducing a separate mask token sequence. Finally, we refine the model through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with contract-guided, region-aware rewards, and apply TraceFusion at inference to preserve high-fidelity content outside the effective edit region. Across six public benchmarks and the proposed LensErase-Bench, LensErase achieves substantial improvements under both reference-based objective metrics and reference-free VLM evaluation. We hope LensErase can serve as a foundational model for erase-related applications and systems.

items.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
items.summary: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. items.abstract: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. We post-train Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it through self-play and evaluate transfer to seven unseen natural-language collaboration tasks. CoSIR achieves the highest aggregate score, while its performance in general tasks remains competitive. Behavioral analyses show increased disclosure of private evidence and fewer judged failures to use teammates' input.

items.abstract: Scaling interactive environments is important for training long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning. These environments often require further testing and refinement after initial generation, and correcting defects in a task may also require updating its work context and verifier. However, existing construction pipelines offer limited support for such iterative refinement while keeping these components aligned. We introduce WorkRover, a framework for training long-horizon cowork agents through recursive environment evolution. Its harness-driven synthesis enables construction agents to jointly build and validate semantically aligned work contexts, executable tasks, and evidence-grounded verifiers, adapting their actions to workspace state and execution feedback rather than following a fixed construction workflow. To support environment evolution, we introduce Factorial Compatibility Replay (FCR), which uses rollout feedback to evaluate combinations of component revisions through dependency-closed replay and selects the smallest validated repair among tested candidates while preserving task requirements and evaluation constraints. To provide finer-grained training signals, we propose Verifier-to-Turn Credit Assignment (VTCA), which augments trajectory-level GRPO advantages with signals from deterministic workspace-progress checks and assigns a bounded share of positive-progress credit to prerequisite turns using recorded tool-output and artifact dependencies. Using WorkRover, we post-train Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to obtain WorkRover-35B-A3B and evaluate it on several cowork-agent benchmarks. Its reported scores exceed those of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B by 26.27 percentage points on JobBench, 29.32 percentage points on OfficeQA Pro, and 413.25 Elo points on GDPval v2. These results suggest that WorkRover offers a promising foundation for scalable training of long-horizon cowork agents.

items.title: Fish Audio Drama 3 Technical Report
items.summary: We introduce Fish Audio Drama 3, an open-source speech generation model that turns text into directed performances, built on a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts backbone that activates 3B parameters per token. It clones voices from multiple references, follows natural-language direction, revises a take when the next turn gives a note, voices multi-character scenes, edits existing speech by infilling, and synthesizes…
items.abstract: We introduce Fish Audio Drama 3, an open-source speech generation model that turns text into directed performances, built on a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts backbone that activates 3B parameters per token. It clones voices from multiple references, follows natural-language direction, revises a take when the next turn gives a note, voices multi-character scenes, edits existing speech by infilling, and synthesizes long-form and streaming audio. Multi-turn revision, scene dubbing, editing by infilling, and streaming text input are new in Drama 3, all in one model. Drama 3 pairs the hybrid linear-attention backbone with a new codebook multi-token-prediction audio decoder that predicts the acoustic codebooks of each frame in dedicated layers that attend over the entire sequence. The model is trained with a three-stage pre-training recipe, instruction fine-tuning, and large-batch reinforcement learning whose only reward is a single learned model of human preference. Its inference engine decodes a single stream at 271 frames per second on one H200, against 177 for Fish Audio S2, although Drama 3 has more than seven times as many parameters. The model weights are available on GitHub (https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech) and Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3), and inference is available through SGLang-Omni (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni). We highly encourage readers to visit https://fish.audio to direct their own performances.

items.title: TacitVLA: Reasoning Vision-Language-Action Models Without Reasoning Latency
items.summary: Textual reasoning before acting has improved vision-language-action (VLA) models, but at the cost of latency: every action conditioned on the reasoning text must wait for autoregressive decoding. items.abstract: Textual reasoning before acting has improved vision-language-action (VLA) models, but at the cost of latency: every action conditioned on the reasoning text must wait for autoregressive decoding. We show that actions do not need to wait for or condition on the generated reasoning to benefit from it, because the reasoning supervision already improves the backbone representation. We introduce TacitVLA, a reasoning VLA whose action expert never attends to the reasoning it generates for the current call. On long-horizon tasks where the reasoning text also serves as episodic memory, it can generate each entry during action execution rather than before acting. We evaluate it in a controlled study on four benchmarks spanning manipulation and autonomous driving, memory and non-memory tasks: RoboMME, RMBench, LIBERO, and PhysicalAI-AV. On all four, TacitVLA matches the performance of its explicit-reasoning counterpart at up to 3.4x lower latency, and matches the latency of the same architecture trained without reasoning at up to +17.1% success. In absolute terms, it surpasses the best previously published results on the RoboMME Counting suite (82.7% vs. 66.8%) and RMBench (77.5% vs. 56.5%), and reaches 72.9% on LIBERO-Plus and a 52.5% scene score on the public split of the PhysicalAI-AV closed-loop driving challenge. Project page: https://tacitvla.github.io.

items.title: JevGPT: Thinking Fast and Slow in Autonomous Research
items.summary: Autonomous research agents must acquire and reason over evidence within a limited budget. Yet relevant sources can remain uninspected or unused, leaving a gap between retrieval coverage and the evidence that informs research. The challenge is to align fast local judgments with changing evidence needs and feed their findings back into research decisions. We introduce JevGPT, a dual-system architecture for autonomous…
items.abstract: Autonomous research agents must acquire and reason over evidence within a limited budget. Yet relevant sources can remain uninspected or unused, leaving a gap between retrieval coverage and the evidence that informs research. The challenge is to align fast local judgments with changing evidence needs and feed their findings back into research decisions. We introduce JevGPT, a dual-system architecture for autonomous research that couples fast evidence processing with deliberative research planning. System Two sets evidence objectives and integrates findings, while System One locates support, assesses relevance, and guides further inspection. Independent source judgments run in parallel; selected original passages inform the next research step. Experiments on fixed-corpus question answering and document ranking show that JevGPT achieves leading task performance, with faster completion and lower cost than comparably effective research agents. Evidence analysis shows broader source inspection and greater coverage of supporting documents in the research loop, highlighting efficient evidence processing as a route to more capable autonomous research.

items.title: Rubrics from the Task, Verdicts from Evidence: Pointwise Rubric Rewards with Tool-Augmented Judges
items.summary: Rubric-based reward models (RMs) evaluate responses against explicit criteria. However, existing methods often derive criteria from observed response candidates, introducing response-induced bias that may limit rubric generalizability. Their judges also struggle with mechanical constraints when relying on reading alone, and commonly used pairwise judges provide only relative preferences, complicating their direct…
items.abstract: Rubric-based reward models (RMs) evaluate responses against explicit criteria. However, existing methods often derive criteria from observed response candidates, introducing response-induced bias that may limit rubric generalizability. Their judges also struggle with mechanical constraints when relying on reading alone, and commonly used pairwise judges provide only relative preferences, complicating their direct use for policy optimization. We propose ReVeR, a pointwise rubric RM that derives hard rules and graded principles by reasoning about the instruction alone and evaluates responses independently through tool-augmented judging. Both components are trained through label-blind distillation, in which preference labels only filter a teacher's outputs, yielding ReVeR-Traces, a large-scale dataset of rubric-reasoning and judging trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that ReVeR outperforms pairwise rubric RMs in average preference accuracy, most clearly on instruction following, as well as in test-time scaling and downstream policy optimization. We further find that generator RL improves preference accuracy while reducing rubric fidelity, and that higher preference accuracy does not necessarily translate into better downstream policies. These findings highlight that rubric fidelity, preference accuracy, and downstream utility are distinct properties, shedding light on future RM research.

items.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
items.summary: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. items.abstract: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Scaling collection across diverse environments, in turn, favors lightweight, portable capture systems. Yet, existing datasets provide only partial views of this coordination. Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system. With an emphasis on professional activities, its continuous recordings align egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations, accompanied by step-level descriptions. To achieve this coverage with sparse body sensing, we develop the Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline. Concretely, reusable calibration fixes participant geometry and sensor attachments before motion inference to disentangle mounting offsets from articulation. A temporal prior then completes unobserved joint motion, while layered constraints promote measurement agreement, temporal continuity, and geometric consistency, properties that motion plausibility alone does not guarantee. Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

items.title: DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multi-turn agents relies on sparse terminal rewards that say little about individual steps. Within-group step comparisons depend on reliable state matching and sufficiently diverse sampled outcomes, while direct step scoring may require costly external evaluators, human annotations, or task-specific heuristics. items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multi-turn agents relies on sparse terminal rewards that say little about individual steps. Within-group step comparisons depend on reliable state matching and sufficiently diverse sampled outcomes, while direct step scoring may require costly external evaluators, human annotations, or task-specific heuristics. We introduce DeltaTTG to learn a reusable progress signal through a shared progress meter, using low-cost supervision from diverse policies' recorded trajectories without task-specific progress rules. Its supervision target, Token-to-Go (TTG), the number of tokens remaining to be generated until task completion, serves as an observable proxy for remaining completion effort. During actor training, changes in the frozen meter's estimates redistribute outcome-derived advantages across steps without altering the reward, preserving each trajectory's advantage sign and token-average scale. On ALFWorld, PaperSearchQA, and BFCLv3, DeltaTTG improves the average score over GRPO by 5.7 and 7.2 points with Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, respectively, outperforms all compared RL baselines on average, and keeps actor-training GPU-hours close to GRPO. Further experiments show improved sample efficiency and out-of-domain performance, and support the meter's ability to distinguish step quality and guide test-time action selection across actor sizes. The code is available at https://github.com/Xuyan923r/DeltaTTG.

items.title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing
items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are appealing for code generation because they can update many tokens in parallel, yet many are optimized for sequence synthesis rather than edit prediction. items.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are appealing for code generation because they can update many tokens in parallel, yet many are optimized for sequence synthesis rather than edit prediction. This setting is poorly matched to modern AI-assisted IDEs, where edit prediction must infer the next code change from recent edits, the current file, and cursor-local context. Such changes are usually sparse and preserve most source tokens, so regenerating a full code segment wastes computation. We propose Diff Diffusion, a diffusion-inspired LLM framework for code editing that predicts edit paths from an original snippet to its revised form. Diff Diffusion represents denoising as structured edit operations, and combines this formulation with multi-stage training and efficient parallel decoding. By focusing computation on changed regions, Diff Diffusion supports accurate low-latency edits and multi-position parallel modification. Across public edit-completion benchmarks, edit-prediction evaluations, and online validation, Diff Diffusion matches or leads autoregressive baselines while delivering 2.78 times faster inference on public edit-completion benchmarks and a 39.0% P50 model-latency reduction in production. This work provides a new modeling perspective for AI applications that require high accuracy and low latency.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
items.summary: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning…
items.abstract: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

items.title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.summary: Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and…
items.abstract: Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and findings. We review 119 papers to explain how methods choose what to evaluate, recover full-benchmark results, and verify their reliability. From this analysis, we develop a taxonomy covering compression within individual benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and during adaptive evaluation, together with work on redundancy and reliability. We compare their information needs, total costs, reliability checks, and limitations. Methods reduce evaluation costs by selecting representative subsets, using cheaper or reusable information, and testing adaptively, but risk poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and sequential delays. The resulting taxonomy and practical guide help researchers choose, validate, and deploy methods for more efficient and reliable LLM evaluation.

We introduce Mission Analysis (MA)-Bench, built on mission analysis, the first step of military operational planning, in which a staff reads the full situation and states the problem before anyone proposes a solution. items.abstract: How well can a language model turn a large, incomplete and partly contradictory body of documents into a plan when no single correct answer exists? We introduce Mission Analysis (MA)-Bench, built on mission analysis, the first step of military operational planning, in which a staff reads the full situation and states the problem before anyone proposes a solution. Its 10 expert-built scenarios pair synthetic packets of ten to twelve documents with 1,257 expert-written pass/fail requirements, each containing information on their source, question type, and importance level. A reasoning-model judge grades each brief against the requirements without seeing the documents; it grades like a fifth credentialed planner, leaving a four-planner panel's agreement unchanged (Fleiss κ 0.42 to 0.41), and a judge from a second provider reproduces the model ranking (Spearman 0.94). Across twenty frontier and open-weights models the best gets 62% of the rubric items right. Models are strongest on facts stated in the documents (58%) and weakest on judgments that must be inferred (33%), and six failures in ten are omissions rather than errors. MA-Bench grades the determinations, not the prose. We release the packets, rubrics, prompts, scorer and every graded brief with item-level verdicts.

items.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use generative visual representations to condition robot actions, yet how these representations organize action-relevant information remains poorly understood. We identify persistent high-norm spatial outliers in WAM representations and find that their action relevance persists even after normalization and K/V projection attenuate their extreme magnitude. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RegisterWAM, which adds learnable non-spatial registers to the world model and uses them directly for action conditioning. Registers alone do not fully eliminate spatial outliers; pairing them with observation flow-matching (FM) loss supervision suppresses spatial outliers while concentrating high-norm responses in registers. Beyond this reorganization, observation FM loss supervision also improves action learning without registers, motivating an additional noised-observation FM objective that learns current-scene recovery from corrupted inputs. The resulting model achieves 81.64\% success on LIBERO-Plus without additional embodied pretraining data or foundation models, reaches 93.0\% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and improves real-world manipulation performance.

items.title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Constructing robust GUI agents relies on multimodal visual grounding: the ability to precisely map natural language intents to actionable on-screen components. Despite abundant desktop, web, and mobile benchmarks, high-fidelity resources tailored for diverse environments are surprisingly scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Screen Referring Grounding Dataset (ScreenRef), a comprehensive GUI grounding dataset…
items.abstract: Constructing robust GUI agents relies on multimodal visual grounding: the ability to precisely map natural language intents to actionable on-screen components. Despite abundant desktop, web, and mobile benchmarks, high-fidelity resources tailored for diverse environments are surprisingly scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Screen Referring Grounding Dataset (ScreenRef), a comprehensive GUI grounding dataset consisting of GUI screenshots paired with natural language referring expressions and box or point annotations. Spanning desktop, web, and mobile domains, ScreenRef comprises 586K screenshots and over 633K referring expression instances, covering tasks such as text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal scenarios. To boost the model's grounding performance, we propose the Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning (D2RL) method to address the limited generalization of supervised fine-tuning and the sparse reward problem in reinforcement learning. Utilizing ScreenRef, we train Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct via sequential SFT and D2RL training, yielding GroundGUI-8B. GroundGUI-8B achieves 95.2% on ScreenSpot-V2, 63.9% on ScreenSpot-Pro, 65.4% on OSWorld-G, 86.8% on MMBench-GUI L2, and 38.3% on UI-Vision. Among 8B-scale models, it produces substantial gains over models trained on open-source datasets, with performance comparable or even superior to models trained on closed-source data. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/PrentisAI/GroundGUI.

items.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
items.summary: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates…
items.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

items.title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning
items.summary: Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. We propose Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP), a model-based framework that…
items.abstract: Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. We propose Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP), a model-based framework that addresses this tension by learning a generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences. Instead of optimizing sequences from scratch, GTP samples candidate sequences from a diffusion prior and refines them using learned dynamics, reward, and value models, enabling efficient trajectory-level reasoning. Across continuous control and long-horizon manipulation tasks, GTP matches or exceeds state-of-the-art model-free, diffusion-policy, and model-based baselines, and remains stable in regimes where strong baselines degrade. Our results suggest that generative models are best understood not as policies, but as structured proposal distributions for planning, offering a new perspective on how to integrate generative modeling with model-based decision-making.
